# Learning goals

- Build an R package.
- Use Rcpp in the package.
- Practice your GitHub skills.

# Lab description

Today we will write an R package that uses `Rcpp`. To do so, we will use a
[template package](https://github.com/UofUEpiBio/egpkg) that has the following
set up:

- Has a single Rcpp function.

- Uses `roxygen2`.

- Uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration.

The R package doesn't have any testing in place and doesn't have coverage checking.

## Before you start

Since the package uses C++ code, you need a compiler. Run the following in R:

```r
pkgbuild::check_build_tools(debug = TRUE)
```

If it reports a problem, install the build tools for your system: the Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS (run `xcode-select --install` in the Terminal), or [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/) on Windows.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Useful commands

These are the functions from the lecture that you will need today. Run them from inside the package project.

| Function | What it does |
|---|---|
| `usethis::use_r("name")` | Creates `R/name.R` and opens it |
| `usethis::use_testthat()` | Sets up the testing infrastructure (run once) |
| `usethis::use_test("name")` | Creates `tests/testthat/test-name.R` and opens it |
| `usethis::use_package("pkg")` | Adds `pkg` to `Imports` in `DESCRIPTION` |
| `devtools::document()` | Updates `man/` and `NAMESPACE` from roxygen comments (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + D). For packages with C++ code, it also compiles the code |
| `devtools::load_all()` | Loads the package so you can try your functions (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + L) |
| `devtools::test()` | Runs the tests (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + T) |
| `devtools::check()` | Runs `R CMD check` (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + E) |
:::

## Question 1: Make sure you can compile the package

Fork the following repository [UofUEpiBio/egpkg](https://github.com/UofUEpiBio/egpkg),
and clone it to your local computer. Once you have a copy, do the following:

1. Inspect its contents and the file located at `.github/workflows`.

2. GitHub does not run workflows on forks until you allow it. Go to the **Actions** tab of your fork and click the button to enable workflows. Otherwise, nothing will happen when you push.

3. Make sure you can install it using RStudio.

4. Run R CMD check using RStudio.

5. Run R CMD check using the command line (if available).

If you don't fork it and instead downloaded it manually, make sure you 
set up a GitHub repository in your account to push your changes.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hints for Question 1

- In RStudio, both install and check are in the **Build** pane (Install, and More > Check).

- On the command line, go to the folder that *contains* `egpkg/` and run:

  ```shell
  R CMD build egpkg
  R CMD check egpkg_1.0.tar.gz
  ```
:::

## Question 2: Adding a plot function

Here is a function and an example of how to use it:

```r
# Here is the function
myplot <- function(x, y) {

  if (!is.numeric(x) | !is.numeric(y)) {
    stop("x and y must be numeric")
  }

  plot(x, y, col = "blue", pch = 19, cex = 2)

  invisible(
   list(
     x = x,
     y = y
   )
  )

}

# Here is an example
set.seed(312)
x <- rnorm(100)
y <- rnorm(100)
myplot(x, y)
```

Add the function to the package. Notice that you will need to:

1. Add **only the function** to the `R` folder (not the example code).
2. Document it using roxygen2.
3. Add the example to the documentation (using the `@examples` tag).
4. Declare the `graphics` package as a dependency (because of the `plot` function).
5. Add a test for checking that the error message is thrown when the input is not numeric.

Run `devtools::check()` to make sure everything works. Remember to commit and push your changes.

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hints for Question 2

- `usethis::use_r("myplot")` creates `R/myplot.R`. Code outside of functions in the `R` folder runs every time the package is loaded, which is why the example goes under `@examples`.

- The roxygen block needs at least a title, `@param`, `@return`, and `@export`.

- Declaring `graphics` takes two steps:
  - In `NAMESPACE`: either write `graphics::plot()` in the function, or add `#' @importFrom graphics plot` to the roxygen block.
  - In `DESCRIPTION`: run `usethis::use_package("graphics")` to add it to `Imports`.

- The package doesn't have tests yet. First run `usethis::use_testthat()`, then `usethis::use_test("myplot")`. The `expect_error()` function checks that an error is thrown, and can also check its message.

- Run `devtools::document()` after changing roxygen comments.
:::

## Question 3: Adding a C++ function

Add the `ps_match` function [we wrote on Week 5](https://github.com/UofUEpiBio/PHS7045-advanced-programming/issues/8#issuecomment-1424974938).
The linked comment has three versions (`ps_match1`, `ps_match2`, and `ps_match3`). Use `ps_match1` and rename it to `ps_match`.

1. Add the function in a separate C++ file in the `src` folder. Make sure to document
it using `roxygen`. Once you finish that, ensure it compiles and the function
is visible. (then commit and push)

2. Write an example with artificial data passing a random vector with ten elements
   distributed U[0, 1]. Add the example to the documentation using the `@examples` tag. (then commit and push)

3. Write a test using the `testthat` R package. The C++ function should match the results of the equivalent R function:

   ```r
    set.seed(1231)
    x <- cbind(runif(20))

    ps_matchR <- function(x) {
    
    match_expected <- dist(x) |> as.matrix()
    diag(match_expected) <- .Machine$integer.max
    indices <- apply(match_expected, 1, which.min)
    
    list(
        match_id = as.integer(unname(indices)),
        match_x  = x[indices]
    )
    
    }
   ```

(then commit and push)

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Hints for Question 3

- Leave out the `/*** R ... */` block at the end of the Week 5 code. It only works with `Rcpp::sourceCpp()`.

- In C++ files, roxygen comments start with `//'` (not `#'`) and go above the `// [[Rcpp::export]]` line. Follow the format in `src/rcpp_hello_world.cpp`.

- `devtools::document()` (Ctrl/Cmd + Shift + D) compiles the C++ code and updates the documentation and `NAMESPACE`. Then run `devtools::load_all()` and try `ps_match(runif(10))`.

- For the test, create the file with `usethis::use_test("ps_match")` and put the R code above at the top of it. Then compare the two functions inside a `test_that()` block. `expect_equal()` will be useful here.
:::

## Question 4: Check out the coverage of the package (if time permits)

Using the `covr` R package, check out the coverage using the following function

```r
covr::package_coverage()
```
